title: The chariot of fire (2 Kings 2:1–14)
hook: Elisha won't leave Elijah and asks for a double portion of his spirit

segments.voice: Yesterday, Naboth's vineyard, and a prophet who told a king, I have found thee. Your line was not for sale. What did you do for someone losing their place? Day seven hundred thirty-five.

Two men are on the road out of Gilgal, an old prophet and the student who follows him. Elijah stops and says, "Tarry here, I pray thee." Stay here. The LORD has sent me on to Bethel. Something is about to happen, and everyone seems to know it. At Bethel, a company of prophets comes out and asks Elisha: don't you know the LORD will take your master from you today? His answer is short: "Yea, I know it; hold ye your peace." I know. Don't talk about it. And then Elijah says it again: tarry here. And again. Today, the chariot of fire.

Three times Elijah tells him to stay behind: at Gilgal, at Bethel, at Jericho. And three times Elisha gives the same answer, in the King James words: "As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee." So they walk on together to the Jordan. Elijah takes his mantle, his cloak, rolls it up, and strikes the water, and it parts, and the two of them cross on dry ground. On the far side, Elijah finally turns to him: "Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee." Elisha doesn't hesitate, and he doesn't ask small: "I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me." Some readers hear an echo of the law in Deuteronomy, where the firstborn son receives a double portion: Elisha is asking to be his heir. Elijah is honest: "Thou hast asked a hard thing." But if you see me when I'm taken, it will be yours. Then, as they walk and talk, a chariot of fire and horses of fire come between them, "and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven." The text is exact here: the chariot parted them, and the whirlwind took him up. Elisha sees it, and cries out, "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof." He tears his own clothes in two. Then he picks up the mantle that fell from Elijah, walks back to the Jordan, and strikes the water with the same cloak, asking, "Where is the LORD God of Elijah?" And the water parts. The one who wouldn't leave is the one left holding the mantle. He stayed to the end, he asked plainly, and he saw.
screen: `I WILL NOT LEAVE THEE, THREE TIMES.`
`WHERE IS THE LORD GOD OF ELIJAH?`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: bring a teacher to mind. Settle, and breathe. Think of someone who taught you how to live, or how to work, or how to believe: a parent, a coach, a pastor, a boss, a grandparent. If they're still here, ask yourself what you'd want to ask of them, plainly, before it's too late: their blessing, a word about what they see in you, a thank-you they've never heard. If they're gone, ask what mantle they left in your hands. If you pray, you can give thanks for them by name. The bell holds the time.
The chariot of fire. Elisha refuses to leave his teacher, asks for a double portion of his spirit, and sees him taken up by a whirlwind.

Your line: I will not leave you. This week ran from a kingdom torn in two, through ravens, a widow's jar, fire on Carmel, a broom tree and a stolen vineyard, to a chariot of fire. Today, reach out to one teacher, and ask for their blessing in plain words. Day seven hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Some Christians speak of 'passing the mantle' when one generation of leaders hands on to the next, and some churches echo Elisha's request for a double portion when they pray for new leaders.

original.note: Hebrew: a cloak or mantle; Elijah's mantle parts the Jordan, and then falls to Elisha (2 Kings 2:8, 2:13).

trapdoor: what you thought: Elijah rides a flaming chariot into the sky.
what it means: a student who won't leave, asks plainly for his teacher's spirit, and is left holding the mantle.
what a scholar hears: the text says Elijah went up by a whirlwind, the chariot parting them (2:11); some readers link the double portion to the firstborn's share (Deuteronomy 21:17).
